text: Georgi Ivanov Peev (Bulgarian: Георги Пеев; born 11 March 1979) is a Bulgarian former footballer who played as a midfielder. A youth product of Lokomotiv Sofia, he spent three seasons in the Bulgarian A Group with the first team before transferring to Dynamo Kyiv, where he won six major honours. He was discovered at the age of 21 by Dynamo Kyiv manager Valery Lobanovsky while playing for Lokomotiv and signed for €2.5 million. He also played for FC Dnipro Dnipropetrovsk. Peev made his official debut for Lokomotiv in a match against Litex Lovech on 8 August 1998, playing 13 minutes as a substitute, and scored his first professional goal on 5 December 1998 against Spartak Varna in the 10th minute. He was capped 45 times from his debut in 1999, appearing at the UEFA Euro 2004, and featured in 40 games for Bulgaria between 1999 and 2007. A right back or right winger known for his pace and attacking attitude, he was part of the Bulgarian squad at the 2004 European Football Championship, which exited in the first round, finishing bottom of Group C after topping Qualifying Group 8 in the pre-tournament phase. In January 2007, he moved to Amkar Perm in Russia for a reported fee of €500,000. In 2008, he was named fans' favorite player of the Russian Premier League and received a rare revolver from 1936 used by the Red Army. On 10 May 2010, following strong performances for his club, he was recalled to the national team for a friendly match against Belgium. On 27 March 2011, Georgi Peev announced his retirement from international football. His brother Daniel Peev is also a professional footballer.
